Assistant A's answer is wrong in several ways. It rejects arrays of different lengths, even though the task is specifically about different sizes. It sorts the inputs, which takes O(n log n) time, yet it then claims the function runs in O(n). Its median calculation is also incorrect for two arrays, since it just averages the middle elements of each array. The explanation contradicts itself as well.

Assistant B's answer is correct. Its claim that the task is impossible is wrong, because a linear-time, constant-space solution does exist: merge the two arrays with two pointers until the middle is reached. That said, B delivers a binary-search solution that is faster than what was asked (O(log(min(n, m)))) and uses O(1) space, so it satisfies the constraints. The implementation is a correct, standard partition-based algorithm. The only flaw is the opening statement that the requirement can't be met, which is misleading, but the code still meets the constraints, since O(log n) is within O(n).

B is clearly better.
